thesis: Every published bull case for emerging markets rests on a weaker dollar, and the Fed is about to hike into a 3.4% inflation print. That is the single cleanest contradiction in the book: we bought the dollar-down trade in the week the dollar-up catalyst got confirmed. 63-day momentum of +1.0% says the market has already noticed.
bull_case: The structural case is well supported. EM ETFs are effectively a short-dollar position, and after the dollar's sharpest annual decline in eight years in 2025, Morgan Stanley expected further weakness into mid-2026 - a dual tailwind of local-currency gains and price appreciation for US holders. China is about 25% of EEM and analysts forecast 15% earnings growth for MSCI China companies in 2026. JPMorgan projects up to $50B into emerging debt funds this year, and both Morgan Stanley and Bank of America have upgraded the asset class. The revival has breadth rather than one story behind it: a weaker dollar, resilient semiconductor demand lifting Taiwan and Korea, and renewed foreign flows into China and India. Packet: close > SMA50 > SMA200, ATR 1.3%, and the position is +1.2%.
bear_case: The central assumption is being falsified in real time. Those dollar forecasts were written expecting Fed easing; instead August CPI came in at 3.4% with core above estimate, and the Fed is priced to hike on 16 September. A hiking Fed with US 2-year yields at their highest since January 2025 is a dollar-positive setup, which removes the main support under EM. The China leg needs Beijing to deliver effective stimulus, and the same Chinese economy is showing only ~30% of steelmakers profitable and a public trade fight with the G20 over export reliance. Momentum is the tell: +1.0% over 63 days and a score of +0.36, the weakest in the book - this entered on the trend filter, not on strength. August CPI landed this morning and settled the argument: headline +0.4% m/m and 3.4% year on year, core +0.3% m/m against a 0.2% estimate, with gasoline up 3.9% and accounting for over a third of the monthly increase. Hike odds for 15-16 Sep jumped on the print - sources put them anywhere from ~69% to 85-90%, but every one of them agrees the direction is a hike being priced. The fed funds rate has sat at 3.5-3.75% all year.
catalysts: 15-16 Sep 2026 FOMC and the dollar's reaction
Chinese stimulus measures and Q3 data
MSCI China earnings delivery against the 15% forecast
risks: A hiking Fed is dollar-positive, removing EM's main tailwind
The bull case rests on dollar forecasts written for an easing Fed
~25% China weight dependent on stimulus execution
63d momentum +1.0%, the weakest score in the book at +0.36
invalidation: Flips long on a close above 71 with the dollar index falling *after* the 16 September FOMC - dollar weakness through a hike would be genuine evidence. The bear case confirms on a close below 64.50, which breaks the SMA50 and the summer range.
